original_value: In the contemporary scientific world, unpredictable health‐related issues and tribulations are changing into new diseases for the next generation. Medication and its treatment levels have advanced to the next level to support the human race. A patient's regular health check‐up in hospices and continuous guidance from a practitioner are added as habitual in a typical human life. However, it might not support patients who escalate to critical care in a fraction of minutes. As a sustaining connotation for healthcare, body sensors (BS) have been espoused for the regular monitoring the patients; irrespective of the patient's daily activities, BS follows him or her like a shadow without his or her intervention. The sensed information is transmitted to the medication department exclusively, and it is expected to reach the concerned practitioner, most importantly without delay and intervention. The health information which are generated at critical situations, have to be traversed to reach the healthcare system. There is a need for network miniaturization to process the patient health information. There are issues pertaining to data forecasting of the base station or healthcare management system. This paper particularly focuses on the coordinator‐specific optimized healthcare monitoring through patient data forwarding during normal, emergency, and critical cases. However, if every patient has his or her own device, that is, bring your own devices (BYODs), then there arises a data privacy problem for sharing resources in BYODs. For organizing the smart device resources, there might be an optimization technique to allocate resources in the network frame due to its mobility and ad hoc nature. To perform the resource allocation process, the proposed system adopts the artificial bee colony approach for the evolution of information collected from the patient's sensors for a precautionary medication process. The efficiency of the proposed system is evaluated using existing techniques. The experimental result analysis shows that the proposed system performance is high in all scenarios, and moreover, it maintains a high reliability rate in delivering sensitive data more effectively.

result.paraphrase: This paper examines coordinator-specific, optimized healthcare monitoring through forwarding patient data in normal, emergency, and critical cases. In contemporary healthcare, unpredictable health issues are driving the need for advanced medication support, regular checkups, and continuous practitioner guidance, though these may fail when patients deteriorate rapidly. Body sensors are used to monitor patients continuously without interrupting daily activities, transmitting sensed information directly to the medical department and, ideally, to the concerned practitioner without delay. Since critical health information must be routed to the healthcare system, network miniaturization is needed to process patient data, and forecasting issues arise in the base station or healthcare management system. With BYOD environments, data privacy becomes a concern when sharing resources, and resource allocation in the network frame requires optimization because of mobility and ad hoc behavior. To manage smart-device resources, the proposed system uses the artificial bee colony approach to evolve sensor-collected information for precautionary medication. Its efficiency is compared with existing techniques, and the experimental results show strong performance across all scenarios, along with high reliability in delivering sensitive data more effectively.
